main_text.p: quo impleto demum, amplius non nubent, neque ducent, sed erunt sicut angeli Dei in coelo, Matth.22.Luc.14. Generant & concubinarii & scortatores, sed de hujusmodi generatione glorientur spurii & conjugii contemptores. Nec voluit Deus per inordina-tam hanc & liberam libidinem & turpitudi-nem propagari genus humanum [?]. Et fures, satiantur, de pane furto acquisito, & veste furto ablata refocillantur. Nemo tamen dixerit, furto quaerendum esse victum & amictum;

Tertiò institutum est, ut hoc modo vagæ libidines, adulteria, stupra, fornicationes, & omnes immunditiæ, quas Deus ut mens casta & sancta extremè abominatur, vitentur, sicut scriptum est, 1.Corinth.7. Nam sine conjugii remedio, promiscuæ & vagæ libidines coerceri nequeunt. Unde & Theophyl. Ecce, inquit, preciosas nuptias, honorabile matrimonium nominat, quod in temperantia ho-minem conservet. Et Metellus Numidicus, A. Gellio teste in 1.cap.6. Si (inquit) sine uxo-ribus possemus esse, omnes ea molestia care-remus (ac, ut Cato dicebat, vita nostra non esset absq; diis) sed quoniam ita natura tra-didit, ut nec cum illis satis commodè, nec si-ne illis ullo modo vivi possit, saluti perpe-tuæ potius, quàm in brevi voluptati consulen-dum est. page.notes: Long s was read as plain s throughout (e.g. "fine" = sine, "fatis" = satis, "faperent" = saperent, "fcortatores" = scortatores). "Et fures": the initial letter may be a long s; kept as printed. "propagarigenus" appears to be "propagari genus" with the space lost in print; kept as printed, not corrected. "Tertiò" has a grave accent as printed. A faint mark precedes "Tertiò" and faint show-through of marks appears between the lines of the first paragraph; these were not transcribed. Reference "1.cap.6." uses the printed numeral 1 (possibly I). The paragraph ends with the hyphenated word "judi-", which continues on the next page.
